purpose: The assembled production React page measured the way the pre-React baseline was measured, against the budgets that receipt fixes.
cohort_sizing: Controlled synthetic 5/50/250 cohorts. The median label is the middle scenario, not a measured real-user median.

methodology.paint: Actual /api/data fetch start to two animation frames after the fixture title is rendered; a frame boundary proxy, not compositor presentation time.
methodology.updateTrigger: The page's own fallback-poll callback (the 20 s setInterval the live transport registers), captured from setInterval and invoked: the production background-poll path, including its focus/open-choice paint deferrals; no manual refresh bypass. The React page has no global poll function to call as the baseline did.
methodology.browserProfile: One fresh owned profile per invocation. Each cohort gets one new-document load per invocation; later cohorts share cache with earlier cohorts. Repeat invocations for independent profiles, not independent cold-cache cohorts.
methodology.observers: Main-window fetch/timer/WebSocket wrappers, primitive MutationObserver counts and long-task observer, identical to the baseline's, plus two declared additions: the setInterval wrapper keeps each callback (to invoke the poll) and an EventSource wrapper counts open streams.
methodology.sockets: WebSocket instances only; TCP/socket descriptors are unavailable.
methodology.retention: Removed node observations and CDP DOM counters are trends, not proof of retained detached-node memory.
methodology.statePaint: Empty/unavailable have no unique sequence marker in production DOM; update-to-paint unavailable.

differences_from_baseline: The page is react.html through frontend_fluidity_fixture.py, which serves the baseline fixture's data and states (its cohorts, rows, titles and states); the baseline's own fixture script was removed with the previous interface.
The poll is the page's own 20 s fallback-poll callback, captured from setInterval; the React page has no global poll function.
Two instrumentation additions: the setInterval wrapper keeps callbacks and an EventSource wrapper counts open streams. The shared instrumentation is otherwise the baseline's text, checked by a test.
The editor step also holds an opened disclosure and the prompt select and checks native undo.
A second navigation series is read after a forced collection, taken after the baseline-comparable one so it cannot disturb it.
The navigation series runs in a document that holds the live stream (the lease is dropped and re-taken), so the stream count means something.
Ports come from the migration's own list; 4571 is not used.

environment.comparability: Same platform and architecture. Chrome moved from Chrome/156.0.8078.4 to Chrome/156.0.8078.12 (same major) and Node from v26.8.2 to v26.10.0; the baseline's own receipt says its timings are not compared across machines or browsers. The control block is historical and cannot be re-measured after retirement.

baseline_status: Historical. The pre-React baseline's probe and fixture were removed with the previous interface, so it cannot be re-measured: its budgets derive from the runs embedded in docs/frontend-baseline.json, which is bound here by digest, and its control runs are kept as they were taken.

page.terminal_note: The optional xterm script and stylesheet are served separately on first use and are accounted apart from the core page, as they were for the legacy page.

budget_policy.timing: Same browser, machine, driver and cohort order only. Median times 1.5 plus 50ms allows runner noise; cross-machine timings are not compared to these absolute limits.
budget_policy.core_html: Re-based by the owner on 2026-10-10 from the baseline's 25% growth to a fixed ceiling, because the page is served locally and the time budgets are the guard; the optional terminal packaging is accounted apart, as before.
budget_policy.resource_counts: Main-window timers, WebSockets and listener counts must settle after navigation; CDP raw node growth alone is not a retained-memory proof. EventSource/TCP/detached-node coverage remains unavailable here and needs separate behavioral transport tests.

scope_limits: Each run starts a fresh owned browser profile; later cohorts load new documents in that same profile and may share browser/font caches.
Two animation frames after the rendered marker is a frame-boundary proxy, not compositor presentation.
Native goal typing, caret and focus were measured; correction undo, IME and open-select behavior remain required browser checks in their migration issues.
Flat synthetic session cohorts do not model every worker/history/reading shape; those remain in the ownership and parity inventory.
Each run starts a fresh owned browser profile; the three cohorts of one run share it.
TCP descriptors and retained detached nodes are not observed and are not reported as zero.
A native select popup cannot be opened through the debugger protocol here; the open-popup hold is proven by the controls browser proof named in the cutover receipt.

verdicts.statistic: total long-task ms over the three runs; derived, the baseline states none
total long-task ms over the three runs; derived, the baseline states none
total long-task ms over the three runs; derived, the baseline states none

verdicts.limit: every counter constant across the navigation rounds
verdicts.statistic: a forced collection before every reading, so a count that only rises until the next collection is not retention

gc_pending.ruling: Ruled by the migration lead at cutover review on 2026-10-09, under the owner's standing delegation; the owner has not reviewed it. Resource counts must settle rather than grow with navigation, and retained growth is what matters, so the settle criterion is evaluated after a forced collection before each reading. The series read with no collection forced is recorded here as gc_pending, informational and not a budget, beside the legacy page's own raw series.

removed_nodes_note: Removed-node counts are trends: the baseline kept only a cumulative total, so this is reported, not budgeted.

methodology.sockets: WebSocket instances only; TCP/socket descriptors are unavailable.
methodology.retention: Removed node observations and CDP DOM counters are trends, not proof of retained detached-node memory.
